title: Targeting Mitochondrial Complex I Deficiency in Parkinson’s Disease Models by Transducing NDI1 Gene
author: Li, Zhang, et al.
materials: Cells were seeded on slides in 24-well plates and incubated with 100 nM Mito-Tracker Red CMXRos (ThermoFisher Scientific) at 37 °C for 30 min. The cells were then fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde for 30 min, permeabilized with 0.1% TritonX-100 for 10 min, and then blocked for 1 h. Subsequently, the cells were incubated with 1:100 HA antibody (cat#3724, Cell Signaling Technology) at 4 °C for 16–18 h, followed by incubating with Alexa fluo 647-labeled goat anti-mouse IgG antibody (1:500; Beyotime), and finally observed under a laser scanning confocal microscope (Nikon A1).

SN and striatum tissues from paraformaldehyde-perfused mouse brain tissues were fixed in 4% formaldehyde at 4 °C overnight. H&E staining of slices was performed with H&E staining kit (Beijing Solarbio). The immunohistochemical methods have been previously described by our research group [20]. The primary antibodies used in this study included anti-mouse tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) antibody (1:1000, Immun Star), anti-mouse GFAP antibody (1:1000, Abcam), anti-mouse Iba-1 antibody (1:1000, Abcam) or anti-mouse NeuN antibody (1:1000, Sigma). Three fields were taken randomly from one slice of four different slices for each group, and the average value was calculated.

To verify the alternative compensation effect of NDI1 on MPP+-induced defective mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, the overall oxygen consumption level, complex I-dependent oxygen consumption level, and ATP level were measured. For the overall mitochondrial oxygen consumption, the basal oxygen consumption in MPP++vector group was decreased significantly in comparison with H2O + vector group (P < 0.001), whereas it was significantly higher in MPP++NDI1 group than in MPP++vector group (P < 0.001)(Fig. 2A, Base). After ATP synthase (complex V) was inhibited by oligomycin, the oxygen consumption was lower significantly in MPP++vector group than in H2O + vector group (P < 0.05) or MPP++NDI1 group (P < 0.001), and MPP++NDI1 group had a completely recovered level in comparison with H2O + vector group (Fig. 2A, Oligo). The result of maximum oxygen consumption (Fig. 2A, FCCP), detected after the respiratory chain uncoupler FCCP was added, was similar as Oligo (Fig. 2A, Oligo). The results indicated NDI1 could restore MPP+-impaired oxygen consumption levels to a certain extent. Furthermore, the respiratory control rate (RCR) and leakage control rate (LCR) were used to respectively evaluate the oxidative phosphorylation coupling efficiency and proton leakage of mitochondria. RCR in MPP++vector group was significantly lower than that in H2O + vector group (P < 0.001), and it was increased in MPP++NDI1 group than in MPP++vector group (P < 0.05) (Fig. 2B). LCR was higher in MPP++vector group than H2O + vector group (P < 0.01) and MPP++NDI1 group (P < 0.05) (Fig. 2C).

steps.title: Culture neuronal and packaging cells
steps.instruction: Maintain SH‑SY5Y neuronal cells and 293T‑17 packaging cells in Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium (Gibco) supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum (Gibco) at 37 °C in a humidified incubator with 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Seed cells for immunofluorescence
steps.instruction: Place cells onto glass slides placed in 24‑well plates and allow them to adhere overnight before staining.

steps.title: Label mitochondria with Mito‑Tracker
steps.instruction: Incubate the cells with 100 nM Mito‑Tracker Red CMXRos (ThermoFisher Scientific) at 37 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Fix and permeabilize cells
steps.instruction: Fix cells with 4 % paraformaldehyde for 30 min at room temperature, then permeabilize with 0.1 % Triton X‑100 for 10 min.

steps.title: Block and incubate primary antibody
steps.instruction: Block non‑specific binding for 1 h (buffer not specified), then incubate with HA antibody (cat#3724, Cell Signaling Technology) diluted 1:100 at 4 °C for 16–18 h.

steps.title: Incubate secondary antibody and image
steps.instruction: Add Alexa Fluor 647‑conjugated goat anti‑mouse IgG (1:500; Beyotime) for the appropriate time, wash, and observe the slides using a Nikon A1 laser‑scanning confocal microscope.

steps.title: Fix mouse brain tissue for histology
steps.instruction: Perfuse mouse brains with paraformaldehyde, then post‑fix dissected substantia nigra and striatum slices in 4 % formaldehyde at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Perform H&E staining
steps.instruction: Stain the fixed brain sections with a Hematoxylin‑Eosin staining kit (Beijing Solarbio) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Conduct immunohistochemistry
steps.instruction: Apply primary antibodies diluted 1:1000: anti‑mouse tyrosine hydroxylase (TH, Immun Star), anti‑mouse GFAP (Abcam), anti‑mouse Iba‑1 (Abcam), or anti‑mouse NeuN (Sigma). Follow with appropriate secondary antibodies and detection as previously described by the authors.

steps.title: Measure overall oxygen consumption
steps.instruction: Using a cellular respiration analyzer, record basal oxygen consumption, then add oligomycin to inhibit ATP synthase (complex V) and record the oligomycin‑treated rate, and finally add the uncoupler FCCP to obtain the maximal rate.

steps.title: Assess complex I‑dependent respiration
steps.instruction: Permeabilize cells with digitonin, add the complex I substrates malic acid and glutamic acid, and measure oxygen consumption.

steps.title: Differentiate endogenous vs NDI1 respiration
steps.instruction: First add rotenone (specific mammalian complex I inhibitor) to the assay, then add flavone (general complex I inhibitor) and record the sensitivity of respiration to each inhibitor.

steps.title: Determine cellular ATP levels
steps.instruction: Measure basal ATP concentration, then treat cells with oligomycin and measure the oligomycin‑sensitive ATP fraction; calculate the ratio oligomycin‑sensitive / basal.

steps.title: Quantify mitochondrial ROS
steps.instruction: Stain cells with MitoSOX™ according to the kit instructions, analyze fluorescence by flow cytometry, and record ROS levels.

steps.title: Detect caspase cleavage by Western blot
steps.instruction: Extract protein from cells, run SDS‑PAGE, transfer to membrane, and probe with antibodies against cleaved caspase‑9 and cleaved caspase‑3 to assess mitochondrial‑mediated apoptosis.
